faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the ORB Male × NPT Male Connector?

The table shows 5,000 psi at dash 2 (1/8" tube) and 1,500 psi at dash 32 (2" tube) for union and bulkhead ends, with 5,000 and 1,000 psi where a pipe thread is on the fitting. faqs.q: What is the ORB Male × NPT Male Connector made from, and when should I choose stainless over carbon steel?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel ORB Male × NPT Male Connector is made from 316L stainless steel, forged. 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316, which suits sea water and chloride-bearing service. Stainless is chosen where zinc-plated carbon steel would corrode, as in offshore and marine lines, chemical and petroleum plant, and food and beverage process equipment. The zinc-plated carbon steel version is listed separately as Steel ORB Male × NPTF Male Adapter. Tell us the fluid and temperature if the medium is unusual.

faqs.q: Which standards does the ORB Male × NPT Male Connector follow, and can I get certificates?
faqs.a: The ORB Male × NPT Male Connector is listed to SAE J1926, ISO 11926 and ASME B1.20.1. They cover straight-thread O-ring ports and general-purpose inch pipe threads. This listing holds no test certificate or declaration; if your job needs a material certificate, ask for it in the enquiry so it can be requested before supply.

faqs.q: What does the ORB Male × NPT Male Connector connect to?
faqs.a: On the ORB Male × NPT Male Connector, the ORB male end screws into an SAE O-ring boss port and seals on its O-ring. The NPT male thread screws into a female NPT port or fitting. Matching parts: [adapter O-rings shelf](/c/adapter-o-rings).

faqs.q: How do I install the ORB Male × NPT Male Connector without leaks or galling?
faqs.a: To fit the Stainless Steel ORB Male × NPT Male Connector: fit the O-ring, lubricate it lightly and screw the end in until the hex seats; the O-ring seals, so tape is not used. Stainless threads can gall if made up dry, so lubricate them. See our [make-up torque guide](/blog/hydraulic-fitting-make-up-torque).
